source_text: Si anima audierit vocem iuramenti et testis sit et non renuntiaverit, accipiet peccatum. Silentium consciorum reatus est. Veritas in ore ecclesiae.
orientation: Origen is explaining the sin-offering for a soul that hears a public oath and, though a witness, does not speak up.
pass_a_gloss: If [the] soul [shall] have heard [the] voice [of] an oath and [a] witness [it] is and not [it] shall have reported, [it] shall receive sin. [The] silence [of] those who know [is] guilt. [The] truth [is] in [the] mouth [of the] church.

choices.why: Keeps the literal force of accipiet as receiving, matching the legal language of incurring guilt without softening it.
Renuntio here means to make known or declare publicly, not to renounce; the context is a witness failing to speak.
Conscius means one who shares knowledge; rendering it as 'those who know' preserves the participial sense of shared awareness.

choices.english: in the mouth of the church
choices.why: Keeps the bodily metaphor of the mouth as the organ of speech, matching Origen's ecclesial application of the verse.
rejected: on the lips of the church

bible_refs.note: Si anima audierit vocem iuramenti et testis sit et non renuntiaverit, accipiet peccatum

pass_b_english: If a soul has heard the voice of an oath and is a witness and has not reported it, it will receive sin (Leviticus 5:1). The silence of those who know is guilt. Truth is in the mouth of the church.

last_rejected.quote: Truth is in the mouth of the church.
last_rejected.why: English hides that this is Origen's own authoritative statement, not a Scripture quotation.
last_rejected.fix: The truth is in the church's mouth. [Origen's comment, not Scripture]
last_rejected.ruling: Translation accurately renders 'Veritas in ore ecclesiae.' No source markers indicate Origen's own statement vs Scripture quotation.
